panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel shows T1-WI low signal in the left globus pallidus area, which is a known radiological manifestation of enterovirus A71 encephalitis, consistent with the article's subject. B: Panel shows bilateral T2-MI high signal in the bulbar/olive nuclear area, matching the description of brainstem changes associated with Enterovirus A71 encephalitis. C: Panel shows bilateral T2-MI high signal in the bulbar/olive nuclear area, matching the description of brainstem changes associated with Enterovirus A71 encephalitis.

B: Axial T2-weighted MRI showing hyperintensities in the dorsal brainstem region, consistent with the pathology described for Patient 1. C: Sagittal T2-weighted MRI showing hyperintensities in the dorsal brainstem region, consistent with the pathology described for Patient 1. D: Sagittal FLAIR image showing the disappearance of previous spinal cord hyperintensity, indicating improvement related to the acute phase of the disease. E: Axial MRI showing dorsal brainstem T2 hyperintensities in an acute phase patient, consistent with Enterovirus 71 encephalitis. panels.figure_caption: Brain and spinal cord MRI findings. Patient 1 – (A–C): dorsal brainstem and cervical hyperintensities on T2-weighted images. (D): sagital FLAIR image shows disappearance of previous spinal cord hyperintensity. Patient 2—(E–G): dorsal brainstem and cervical diffuse and poorly defined T2-hyperintensities during the acute phase; (H): hyperintense T2 signal of the anterior horn of the cervical spinal cord one week later. Patient 3—(I–K): left frontal cortical hyperintensities (asterisk) in diffusion weighted images (DWI); cervical and lumbosacral hyperintensities on T2-weighted imaging with enhancement on post-gadolinium image. (L): axial DWI at 3 months shows resolution of the previous alterations.

le exanthema and EV-71 had been isolated in the child's stool. Neurological examination of patient 3 revealed motor aphasia, right facial paralysis, flaccid tetraparesis and hyperreflexia. Brain MRI (Figure 1I) revealed a left frontal cortical thickening in fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) images, hyperintense in diffusion weighted images (DWI), with leptomeningeal enhancement. Spinal cord MRI (Figures 1J,K) revealed cervical and lumbosacral lesions. CSF showed pleocytosis and enterovirus PCR was negative. Enterovirus RNA was detected by PCR in stool specimens.
